names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 17 iulie, «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Marina», with the rank words left off.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Ιουλίου, «Αγία Μαρίνα», with the rank word left off. The page's etymology box is headed for the masculine ΜΑΡΙΝΟΣ and does not give her name any other form; its hymns and verses have «Μαρίνα» and the vocative «Μαρῖνα».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 17. јул ст. ст., „Св. муч. Марина.“ — „Св.“ is not a rank, „муч.“ is a rank the folder already covers with the greater `great-martyr`, and nothing else is in the heading at all: no by-name, no see, no place, and the city the body gives is not in the heading. «of Antioch in Pisidia» in the display name is the corpus’s own. `foldchk.py` returns **no holder** and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder, which on a bare forename the corpus carries in several spellings is worth recording.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 iulie — «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Marina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Ιουλίου — «Αγία Μαρίνα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the woman is the folder's own: born at Antioch of Pisidia, daughter of a priest of the idols named Αιδέσιος — doxologia's Edesius — brought up by a Christian woman, and beheaded by the eparch after refusing him. She is none of the corpus's other folders the name sweep raised: `marinus-martyr-17-march`, `marinus-the-elder`, `marana` and the Marcians are other names or other days. The Greek page adds what doxologia's long life did not carry: the year of her birth, 270, and the reign of Claudius II; the eparch's name, Ολύμβριος; her age of fifteen when she told her father she was a Christian, where the Romanian life has her hearing of Christ at twelve; the black dog the dragon turned into in the prison and the hammer she struck it with; the lighted candles she was burned with and the healing of those wounds; and the history of her relics — kept at Constantinople until the Latins took it in 1204, or by other sources at Antioch until 908 and then carried to Italy, and now in Athens in a church of her name, with her hand at the monastery of Vatopedi on Athos. It also names her as patron of Leros, of Heliopolis and of Schinoudi on Imbros. A `dates` object is proposed from the year 270. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints six hymn texts: three apolytikia, a kontakion, a megalynarion and an oikos. The three apolytikia and the kontakion are taken — the first names her and Olymbrios, the second and the kontakion name her, and the third, «Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ», names nobody and is the common of a virgin martyr printed under her name, taken as a common and said here to be one. The megalynarion and the oikos are not taken, because this schema holds only a troparion or a kontakion.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.07.2026 (17. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Марина.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, and **the fullest single life this range has read**. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. The identification is the city and the day: „Родом из Антиохије Писидијске“ is this folder’s own Antioch in Pisidia, which is also saint.gr’s — «Η Αγία Μαρίνα γεννήθηκε στην Αντιόχεια της Πισιδίας» — and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 17 July. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE ONE THING THIS BOOK OFFERS IS A REIGN.** The folder holds `birth` 270 to 270, `attested` off saint.gr’s «στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Κλαυδίου του Β΄, το 270 μ.Χ.», and **no `death` at all** — saint.gr gives none and doxologia gave no year of any kind. This book ends „Посечена беше у време цара Диоклецијана“, she was beheaded in the time of the emperor Diocletian. **A reign is no source for a year**, which has now refused a year off Decius, off Julian the Apostate, off Michael and Theodora, off Trajan and off Claudius in this wave, and the refusal here closes nothing: the folder keeps `no-death`. **It is worth saying that the reign does not even conflict** — Diocletian reigned from 284, a woman born in 270 would have been in her teens or twenties, and the body has her hearing of Christ in her twelfth year — so this is a refusal of a kind of evidence and not of a reading. `types` UNTOUCHED at `great-martyr` and `virgin`. **The heading ranks her only „муч.“**, the plain word, where the folder holds `great-martyr` off doxologia’s «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Marina» — and a lesser rank in one calendar does not take away a greater in another, so nothing is removed; nor is anything added, `great-martyr` already covering it. **`virgin` is not re-earned off the body** — „она се заветоваше никад се не удавати“, she vowed never to marry — the folder holding it already and a body being no warrant. **`wonderworker` is refused for the ninth time in this wave**, the wonders at her monastery standing in the body. No `office`. **No `locations`, and here that is a real decision**: the body names Antioch in Pisidia, Mount Athos and Vatopedi, and a monastery on the mountain of Langa above Lake Ohrid in Albania — four places and three of them about relics, and the folder carries a `birth` with no `death`, which `map-span` would have to answer for. **NO NEW `related` ROWS, AND THE DEDICATION RULE HOLDS TWICE.** Her father who came to hate her for her faith and did not consider her a daughter, the imperial governor Olymvrius who first wanted her for a wife, the devil in the shape of a dreadful serpent, the white dove on the cross and the voice from it, and the Lord Himself appearing with angels before her death are a father, a persecutor, the devil, a vision and the Lord. **The monastery of Saint Marina in Albania and the monastery of Vatopedi are dedications and houses, not relations**, which is §6’s rule and the trap this range has now avoided three times. **WHAT IS NEW IS MOST OF THE ENTRY, AND TWO OF ITS SENTENCES ARE ABOUT MUSLIMS.** At twelve she first heard of the Lord Jesus — how He was incarnate of the most pure Virgin, worked many wonders, accepted death on the cross and gloriously rose — and her young heart was set on fire with love for Him, so that she vowed never to marry and longed with her whole soul to suffer for Christ and to be baptised in the blood of martyrdom. **Her father came to hate her for her faith and did not consider her his daughter.** The governor Olymvrius, learning from her own mouth that she was a Christian, first wished her to be his wife; and when she refused he ordered her to bow to the idols, to which she answered „не ћу се поклонити ни принети жртве бездиханим и мртвим идолима, који нити сами себе познају нити пак знају, да ли их ми чествујемо или бешчествујемо; не дам њима оне части, која припада само Творцу мојему“ — I will not bow nor offer sacrifice to breathless and dead idols, which neither know themselves nor know whether we honour them or dishonour them; I will not give them the honour that belongs to my Creator alone. **Then the prison.** The devil appeared to her first in the form of a dreadful serpent **which engulfed her head**, and when she crossed herself the serpent burst apart and vanished. Then a heavenly light shone round her, and it seemed to her that the walls of the prison vanished together with the roof, and a cross appeared, shining and high, and on the top of the cross a white dove, from which came a voice: „радуј се, Марино, разумна голубице Христова, кћери Сиона вишњега, јер приспе дан твога весеља“ — rejoice, Marina, rational dove of Christ, daughter of the Sion above, for the day of thy gladness is come. **And she was healed by the power of God of all her wounds and pains.** The second day the senseless judge tortured her in fire and in water, and she bore it all „као у туђем телу“, as though in somebody else’s body; and before her death the Lord Jesus appeared to her with angels. **One of her hands is at Vatopedi on the Holy Mountain**; and in Albania, on the mountain of Langa above Lake Ohrid, there is a monastery of Saint Marina with a part of her wonderworking relics, where many wonders have happened and happen still, **witnessed not only by Christians but by Muslims** — so much respect do the Turks have for this holy place that they have never been willing to touch either the shrine or the property of that monastery, and **for a time a Turk was the trustee of it**. **ENTRY 2 IS A RUSSIAN ASCETIC WITH A FULL DOSSIER AND NO FOLDER OF ANY KIND.** „Преп. Леонид Устнедумски.“ — this Russian saint struggled from his youth in several monasteries, in Solovki, in Mirozh and others; at last he founded his own monastery **on the river Luza in the province of Vologda**; he struggled hard until his soul was filled with the light of grace and the power of the Holy Spirit, and as a great lamp drew many to the ascetic life; **and he was called Ustnedumsky because when a poisonous snake once bit him he would neither think nor speak of it, and remained alive** — which is the book’s own etymology of the by-name, „зато што кад га је једном ујела отровна змија, он о томе није хтео ни мислити ни зборити“. Having pleased God he reposed peacefully **on 17 July 1653**, and his relics rest in his own monastery. `ls saints | grep -i ustnedum` returns **nobody**; `grep -i leonid` returns twenty folders and every one of them is a martyr of another country or another century — five twentieth-century Russians named Leonid, the companions of Eleutherius and of Leonides, the father of Origen, and men of Athens, Egypt and Epidaurus — and not one is a founder on the Luza. Ruling 3: **reported, not created.** The entry is five sentences, it carries a day, a year, a province, a river, three monasteries and an etymology, and it is the fullest dossier this range has refused a folder to. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Mielușeaua Ta, Iisuse, Marina, strigă cu mare glas: Pe Tine, Mirele meu, Te iubesc și pe Tine cântându-Te, mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc, și mă împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru Tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără prihană primește-mă pe mine, ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un Milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Mare Mucenițe Marina», Glas 4 — the common of a woman martyr; the doubled «și mă împreună mă îngrop» and the lower-case «ție» are the page's own.

english.text: Your ewe-lamb, Jesus, Marina, cries out with a great voice: You, my Bridegroom, I love, and singing to You I am tormented and crucified with You, and buried with You in Your baptism; and I suffer for You, that I may reign in You; and I die for You, that I may live for You. As an unblemished sacrifice receive me, who offer myself to You with love. At her prayers, as the merciful One, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ἀνδρείαν καὶ φρόνησιν, σὺ κεκτημένη σεμνή, ἀνδρείως κατεπάτησας ὄφιν ἀρχέκακον, Μαρίνα πανεύφημε, ἤσχυνας Ὀλυμβρίου τᾶς πικρᾶς τιμωρίας, εὐφρανας Ἀσωμάτων τᾶς χορείας ἀθλοῦσα, διὸ ἀπαύστως πρέσβευε Χριστῷ, εἰς τὸ σωθήναι ἠμᾶς.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον — the first of three apolytikia on the page of «Αγία Μαρίνα», printed with no ἦχος; it names her and the eparch Olymbrios

english.text: Having gained courage and good sense, modest one, you bravely trod down the serpent that began our evils, all-praised Marina; you put the bitter punishments of Olymbrios to shame, and by your contest you gladdened the companies of the bodiless ones. Therefore intercede unceasingly with Christ, that we may be saved.

hymns.text: Μνηστευθεῖσα τῷ Λόγῳ Μαρίνα ἔνδοξε, τῶν ἐπιγείων τὴν σχέσιν πᾶσαν κατέλιπες, καὶ ἐνήθλησας λαμπρῶς ὡς καλλιπάρθενος· τὸν γὰρ ἀόρατον ἐχθρὸν κατεπάτησας στερρῶς ὀφθέντα σοὶ Ἀθληφόρε. Καὶ νῦν πηγάζεις τῷ κόσμῳ τῶν ἰαμάτων τὰ δωρήματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α', Τόν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the second of three apolytikia on the page of «Αγία Μαρίνα», and it names her

english.text: Betrothed to the Word, glorious Marina, you left behind every tie with things of earth and contended brilliantly as a fair virgin; for you trod down stoutly the unseen enemy when he showed himself to you, prize-winner. And now you pour out upon the world the gifts of healings.

hymns.text: Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ, κράζει μεγάλη τῇ φωνῇ. Σὲ Νυμφίε μου ποθῶ, καὶ σὲ ζητοῦσα ἀθλῶ, καὶ συσταυροῦμαι καὶ συνθάπτομαι τῷ βαπτισμῷ σου· καὶ πάσχω διὰ σέ, ὡς βασιλεύσω σὺν σοί, καὶ θνήσκω ὑπὲρ σοῦ, ἵνα καὶ ζήσω ἐν σοί· ἀλλ᾽ ὡς θυσίαν ἄμωμον προσδέχου τὴν μετὰ πόθου τυθεῖσάν σοι. Αὐτῆς πρεσβείαις, ὡς ἐλεήμων, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ' — the third of three apolytikia on the page of «Αγία Μαρίνα». It names no saint and is the common of a virgin martyr, printed under her name and therefore taken as her service and recorded here as a common

english.text: Your ewe-lamb, Jesus, cries out with a loud voice: You, my Bridegroom, I long for, and seeking You I contend; I am crucified with You and buried with You in Your baptism; and I suffer for Your sake, that I may reign with You, and I die for You, that I may live in You. Receive her then as a spotless sacrifice, offered to You in longing. By her prayers, as You are merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Παρθενίας κάλλεσι, πεποικιλμένη παρθένε, ἀκηράτοις στέμμασιν, ἐστεφανώθης Mαρίνα, αἵμασι, τοῦ μαρτυρίου δε φοινιχθεῖσα, θαύμασι καταλαμπρύνθης τῶν ἰαμάτων, καὶ τῆς νίκης τὰ βραβεῖα, ἐδέξω Μάρτυς χειρὶ τοῦ Κτίστου σου.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ', Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — the one kontakion on the page of «Αγία Μαρίνα», and it names her

english.text: Adorned with the beauties of virginity, O virgin, you were crowned with undefiled crowns, Marina; and reddened with the blood of martyrdom, you were made radiant with the wonders of healings, and received the prizes of victory, martyr, from the hand of your Creator.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Η Αγία Μαρίνα γεννήθηκε στην Αντιόχεια της Πισιδίας, στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Κλαυδίου του Β', το 270 μ.Χ.» The page gives no year for her death, and doxologia.ro, the folder's other source, gave no year at all.
